newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Long bond yields marched lower on Wednesday on healthy buying from across-the-board as investors' appetite for stock re-awakened.
This followed a big shake-out in the market on Monday and Tuesday, debt market traders said.
At 1409 GMT the benchmark R150 loan yielded 14.03 percent from an intraday strongest level of 14.02 percent and 14.13 percent late on Tuesday.
"There were some good institutional buyers, in short, more buying than selling interest," said a senior trader.
The market responded positively to comments in the morning by Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals indicating that the central bank was hopeful of an interest rate cut by year-end, some traders said.
This supported the general feeling that a rate cut was still on the cards within the next month, they said
"I now expect some consolidation around the figure," another trader said, adding that there was still a lot of stock floating aroun.
Players were awaiting July reserves numbers on Friday and the August 7 options close-out.
Foreigners bought a net 380.89 million rands worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 269.30 million on Monday, the Bond Exchange said.
Bond Exchange turnover climbed to 11.62 billion rand on Tuesday from 3.48 billion rand on Monday.
The rand had a slow day, traipsing slightly weaker on a strong dollar as exporters competed with dollar importer demand.
"It's the same story, we're still weakening gradually," commented one trader.
He said the currency had come off at the opening, touching an intraday weakest bid of 4.5940.
At 1409 GMT it was changing hands at 4.5925/5975 on the greenback from 4.5880/5910 at the local Tuesday close.
The dollar surged in Europe, setting a 47-month high against the Swiss franc and hitting an 11-week peak in the yen.
Local dealers said activity had generally been muted and demand for dollars slightly more subdued.
"We're looking semi-toppish for now but nevertheless a test of 4.60 is on the cards quite soon," said another from a leading local institution.
There had been no sign of the central bank, several institutions said.
At 0728 GMT the rand was 4.5885/5915 on the dollar from 4.5880/5910 overnight.
In cross rate action, the rand was last at 7.4610/4737 versus sterling from 7.4753/4848 versus.
Against the mark the local unit was last changing hands at 0.4007/4012 from 0.3987/3992 Tuesday. It was last fetching 25.7879/8225 against the yen from a previous levels of 5.6533/6810.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage fell to 6.587 billion rand on Tuesday from 7.234 billion rand on Monday.

Offered rates for three-month NCDs were slightly lower at between 15.45 to 15.55 percent from 15.55 percent, while the 90-day BA rate also lined up slightly lower at between 14.90 to 15.00 percent from 15.00 percent previously.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
